clue.text: Toy one is wanting priest to hide in part of church

indicators.note: the priest's letter goes into hiding inside what is left of the toy
something wanting is lacking, so the letter for one goes missing from the toy

parts.note: a model railway, a train set, is a classic toy
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A child's plaything is missing, and a clergyman is told to take cover somewhere in the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is wanting' drops I from TRAINSET to leave TRANSET; 'to hide' then tucks P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A transept is the arm crossing the nave in a cross-shaped church building.

clue.text: Bear steak needs to be chewed 28 times?

indicators.note: chewing mangles food, so these letters are mashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A tough cut of bear meat has to be chewed many times over.
explanation.walkthrough: '28' refers to the answer of 28 across, CHITCHAT: tea breaks are times for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaks for a cuppa at work are when colleagues stop for a natter, so times for idle chat.

clue.text: Unfinished parable in which Republican ascends rapidly

indicators.note: in a down answer, rising moves the letter higher, so nearer the start
an unfinished word loses its last letter

parts.note: a parable is a story with a moral, an allegory

explanation.surface: In an unfinished moral tale, a Republican rises fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' trims ALLEGORY to ALLEGOR; 'ascends' moves its R up one place.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is the musical direction to play at a brisk, lively pace.

clue.text: A period of time off to watch Ms Rantzen broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard, so the phrase is taken by its sound

parts.note: to watch is to see, and Esther Rantzen is a long-serving British TV presenter, known for That's Life!

explanation.surface: Taking a break to watch a well-known TV presenter on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' asks for the sound of SEE ESTHER.
explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is an afternoon nap or rest, a break from work in hot countries.

clue.text: Dull argument, but one that brings action

parts.note: plain means ordinary or dull
a tiff is a petty quarrel or argument

explanation.surface: A boring quarrel, yet one that gets things moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'action' here is a lawsuit, not activity.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaintiff is the person who brings a case, or legal action, against another in court.

clue.text: Oil producer abuses American guards

indicators.note: the outer words hold, or guard, the letters sitting inside them

explanation.surface: Someone who makes oil mistreats the Americans who protect them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guards' signals the letters held within 'abuSES AMErican'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sesame seeds are pressed to give an oil much used in Asian cooking.

clue.text: Oozing spot on errand boy

parts.note: to spot is to see
a page is a boy who runs errands, as in a hotel

explanation.surface: A messenger boy with a weeping pimple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spot' looks like a blemish but is the verb to notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Seepage is slow leaking of liquid, the gradual oozing through something.

clue.text: Carol's cuddling Damon, perhaps for cash

indicators.note: one word wraps its arms round the other, holding it inside

parts.note: carols, as a verb, means sings
Damon Hill, the British Formula One world champion, is one example of a Hill

explanation.surface: A woman called Carol hugs a man named Damon, perhaps for money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' reads as a name but is the verb; 'cuddling' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Shillings were coins of old British currency, twelve pence each, so money.

clue.text: Infatuated with cycling in gloves

indicators.note: letters cycle from one end of the word round to the other

parts.note: smitten with someone means infatuated with them

explanation.surface: Someone who loves cycling while wearing gloves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves the S of SMITTEN from front to back.
explanation.definitionFit: Mittens are gloves with one section for the four fingers and another for the thumb.

clue.text: Become sick of beer, say

indicators.note: 'say' asks for the word as spoken rather than as written

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Getting fed up with drinking beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns ALE into the word that sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To ail is to be unwell or fall ill, a slightly old-fashioned verb.

clue.text: Greek who scored in first part of extra time to become preacher

indicators.note: the composer's name goes inside the two picked letters
the opening letter of each of the two following words is taken

parts.note: Vangelis was the Greek composer who scored films such as Chariots of Fire

explanation.surface: A Greek footballer nets early in extra time and becomes a hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scored' suggests a goal, but means writing film music. 'first part of' gives E and T from 'extra time'; 'in' puts VANGELIS between them.
explanation.definitionFit: An evangelist is someone who preaches the gospel, often travelling to do so.

clue.text: Making good literature, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the phrase asks for a word pronounced the same as the synonym

parts.note: writing is a general word for literature

explanation.surface: Good literature, it seems, is being produced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the sound of it' points to the word said like WRITING.
explanation.definitionFit: To right a wrong is to make it good, putting things back as they should be.

clue.text: Numb, a member of flock left for hospital

indicators.note: one letter stands for, or replaces, another

parts.note: a sheep is one animal in a flock
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A sheep, frozen with fear, is left behind in place of one sent to hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is the swap signal: the hospital letter gives way to the one for left.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb that has gone numb is said to be asleep, with pins and needles.

clue.text: Elementary constituent of alpha male

parts.note: alpha is the first Greek letter, the counterpart of A
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: What a dominant male is basically made of.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom is the smallest unit of a chemical element, so a pun on elementary.

clue.text: Maybe Johnson gets friend out of nowhere?

parts.note: Magic Johnson was a star American basketball player, one Johnson among many
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Perhaps a politician named Johnson finds a friend from nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Johnson' suggests the British politician, but here it is the basketball player.
explanation.definitionFit: Appearing as if by a conjuring trick, something arrives inexplicably and suddenly.

clue.text: Swiss capital invested in fruit by son showing flexibility

indicators.note: the capital is put into the fruit, as money is invested

parts.note: limes are a citrus fruit
Bern is the capital of Switzerland

explanation.surface: Swiss money is put into the fruit business by a son with an eye for flexibility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money but is a city; 'invested in' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Limberness is the quality of being supple, bending easily without stiffness.

clue.text: A tiny fraction of account that's charged by brothels, essentially

parts.note: a bill is an account of money owed
an ion is an atom carrying electric charge

indicators.note: the essence, or central letters, of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A small cut of the bill that brothels charge clients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' suggests billing, but ION is a charged particle; 'essentially' takes TH from the middle of 'brothels'.
explanation.definitionFit: One part in a thousand million is a minuscule proportion of a whole.

clue.text: Seen to be worried over smell of old age

indicators.note: in a down answer, over places the first piece on top of the second
to worry something is to fret it out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a scent is a smell

explanation.surface: Visibly anxious about the smell of elderly people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be worried' rearranges the first word to SENE, and 'over' stacks it above the smell in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Senescent describes growing old, the biological ageing of a living thing.

clue.text: Records how the British queue?

definitions.meaning: a file holding singles, seven-inch records, read playfully
the British famously line up one behind another

explanation.surface: A note on how the British stand patiently in line.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is whimsical: a collection of singles is a file of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking one behind another in a line is moving in that formation, as orderly queues do.

clue.text: Heathen at home with revolutionary

parts.note: someone at home is in
Fidel Castro led the Cuban revolution

explanation.surface: A pagan who lives with a rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: An infidel is a non-believer, someone without the faith of the speaker.

clue.text: Twice set out to sequester area for housing developments

indicators.note: to sequester is to isolate or hold apart, so the other letter is enclosed
letters put out of order are rearranged
the word set is used two times over

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Twice, a plan is set out to set aside land for new homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twice' gives SETSET, 'out' rearranges it to ESTTES, and 'to sequester' puts A in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Housing estates are planned areas of homes built together as a single scheme.

clue.text: Runner's last to run and hide

parts.note: a ski is a runner on snow; the possessive 's joins it to what follows

indicators.note: only the final letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A sprinter, finishing last, wants to run off and hide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, but a ski is a runner a sledge slides on; 'last to' takes N from 'run'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hide is an animal's pelt, the same as its skin.

clue.text: Thinks 'European' is weird dialect

indicators.note: something weird is strange or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a European form of speech is odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is weird' rearranges THINKS plus E.
explanation.definitionFit: Kentish was a dialect of Old English spoken in the south-east English county of Kent.

clue.text: As a laugh, picked up swallow

indicators.note: what is picked up is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: done in jest means as a joke, for a laugh

explanation.surface: Jokingly, someone catches a bird in flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' asks for the sound of IN JEST; 'swallow' is the verb, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingest food or drink is to take it into the body by swallowing.

clue.text: Away from home, following football club is boring, it's a bit excessive

indicators.note: something boring drills into, so the other letters sit inside

parts.note: someone not at home is out
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: Following a football club on away trips is dull and rather over the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' reads as dull but means drilling into, the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An offcut is a leftover piece trimmed away as surplus from wood, fabric or paper.

clue.text: They could provide change for the better?

definitions.text: They could provide change for the better?

parts.words: They could provide change for the better?
parts.note: a better is one who bets, and the money a successful gambler collects is cash, or change

explanation.surface: Things that might bring about improvement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the better' looks like improvement but is a person who bets, and 'change' is coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Money paid out to a successful punter at the bookmaker is what they have won.

clue.text: Enthusiastic amateur is talented? It seems otherwise

indicators.note: the letters appear in some other arrangement, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Is a keen hobbyist actually skilled? Apparently not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seems otherwise' rearranges TALENTED plus IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilettante dabbles in an art or interest for pleasure rather than as a professional.

clue.text: That is cold internally

indicators.note: the letter for cold is placed within the abbreviation

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Something that is chilly right through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'internally' puts C within IE; the whole clue also describes frozen water.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen water is cold all the way through, so the clue as a whole describes it.

clue.text: Perhaps mountain is reflected in basins of ephemeral lakes

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: say means perhaps or for example
an alp is a high mountain

explanation.surface: A mountain mirrored in the water of short-lived desert lakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is reflected' turns SAYALP around.
explanation.definitionFit: Playas are flat desert basins that flood briefly after rain and then dry out.

clue.text: Queen possibly conceals problem, leading to gossip

indicators.note: the outer word hides the other inside it

parts.note: a queen is a female cat, so a cat is possibly a queen
a hitch is a snag or problem

explanation.surface: The monarch hides a difficulty, which sets tongues wagging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' suggests royalty but a queen is a breeding female cat; 'conceals' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Chitchat is idle chatter, light talk of the kind spread as gossip.
